# Newton Development repository instructions

## Public-facing copy

- Use direct, professional source/provenance language.
- State where information comes from: official City records, a named agency source, or another clearly identified source.
- Do not use defensive phrasing intended to reassure readers that information was not guessed, invented, made up, or manually estimated.
- Do not add provenance language unless it communicates a useful source or collection method.
- Project facts must be supported by a specific source URL when they are presented as verified facts.

## Automated project data

- Preserve these copy standards when adding or updating projects.
- Prefer omission over filling a project card with an unsupported or unimportant fact.
- Do not manufacture coordinates, dates, costs, counts, statuses, milestones, or event-project relationships.
